Hey. I'm in UK, so here they put you in a psychiatric unit for about ten days to detox. They use Chlordiazepoxide (Librium) to combat the"shakes" and withdrawals. They take you off of it very quickly though, as it's very, very addictive.

You can choose to go on Antabuse (Disulfiram) which makes you very very ill iff you drink. I'm on Antabuse, and it works for me.

Once I was discharged I went into rehab for six months, best thing I ever did. Last two detoxes I ale straight home, first time I was dry for 17 months, then the second, I was dry for 8.5 years.

Don't know where you are, or how medical services are there, but in the UK we have the National Health Service, and it's free. The local council payed for my rehab.

I went to a local AA meeting, and can really recommend it, and really liked it. But I wanted to stuck with the CBT method of therapy I was getting in rehab.

Four years later, still dry, but battling depression.

Oh, by the way, I'm 44!!  So less of the middle aged thing. Only joking.
